transcript_snippet: water boils at a hundred degrees Celsius, um, at sea level anyway, basic chemistry
expected_extraction: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
adjudication_note: 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure.

transcript_snippet: you know we only use like ten percent of our brains, right, imagine if we could unlock the rest
expected_extraction: Humans only use ten percent of their brains.
adjudication_note: Persistent myth; neuroimaging shows virtually all brain regions are active. Universally debunked.

transcript_snippet: light travels at about, uh, three hundred thousand kilometers a second, that's the speed limit of the universe
expected_extraction: The speed of light is about 300,000 kilometers per second.
adjudication_note: c = 299,792 km/s; 'about 300,000' is accurate.

transcript_snippet: look, vaccines cause autism, there's a study, they proved it, that's why people are worried
expected_extraction: Vaccines cause autism.
adjudication_note: The Wakefield study was retracted and fraudulent; large studies find no link. As settled as medical science gets.
source_of_truth: CDC / WHO / retraction of Wakefield 1998 by The Lancet

transcript_snippet: DNA is, um, it's a double helix, the twisted ladder thing, Watson and Crick and all that
expected_extraction: DNA has a double helix structure.
adjudication_note: Established since 1953.

transcript_snippet: if you get a cold just take antibiotics, antibiotics kill viruses, knocks it right out
expected_extraction: Antibiotics kill viruses.
adjudication_note: Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses; colds are viral. CDC runs campaigns against exactly this misconception.

transcript_snippet: the adult human body has two hundred and six bones, uh, babies have more but they fuse
expected_extraction: The adult human body has 206 bones.
adjudication_note: 206 is the standard adult count (minor individual variation exists).

transcript_snippet: you swallow like eight spiders a year in your sleep, that's a real statistic, I hate it
expected_extraction: People swallow about eight spiders a year in their sleep.
adjudication_note: Urban legend with no evidentiary basis; spiders avoid sleeping humans. Often cited as a fact ABOUT misinformation.

transcript_snippet: smoking causes lung cancer, I mean that one's been settled since like the sixties
expected_extraction: Smoking causes lung cancer.
adjudication_note: Settled since the 1964 Surgeon General's report.

transcript_snippet: no sugar for the kids after seven pm because sugar makes kids hyper, every parent knows this
expected_extraction: Sugar makes children hyperactive.
adjudication_note: Controlled studies and meta-analyses find no hyperactivity effect; the belief is expectation bias. Well-documented myth.

transcript_snippet: the Earth is about four and a half billion years old, um, based on the rocks and the dating
expected_extraction: The Earth is about 4.5 billion years old.
adjudication_note: ~4.54 billion years, radiometric consensus.

transcript_snippet: lightning never strikes the same place twice, that's why you're safe after the first one, ha
expected_extraction: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
adjudication_note: Tall structures are struck repeatedly; the Empire State Building takes ~20-25 strikes a year.

transcript_snippet: humans and chimps share like ninety-eight, ninety-nine percent of their DNA, we're basically cousins
expected_extraction: Humans share about 98 to 99 percent of their DNA with chimpanzees.
adjudication_note: ~98.8% sequence identity by the standard comparison; the 98-99% figure is the accepted shorthand.
source_of_truth: Smithsonian Human Origins / NIH comparative genomics

transcript_snippet: goldfish have a three second memory, that's why the little bowl is fine, they forget instantly
expected_extraction: Goldfish have a three-second memory.
adjudication_note: Goldfish demonstrably remember for weeks to months in conditioning experiments.
source_of_truth: Animal cognition literature / widely covered by BBC and Scientific American

transcript_snippet: ibuprofen is an anti-inflammatory, that's the whole point of it, it's not just a painkiller
expected_extraction: Ibuprofen is an anti-inflammatory drug.
adjudication_note: Ibuprofen is an NSAID — nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug.

transcript_snippet: stop cracking your knuckles, you're gonna give yourself arthritis, cracking knuckles causes arthritis
expected_extraction: Cracking your knuckles causes arthritis.
adjudication_note: Studies (including the famous one-hand self-experiment) find no arthritis link.
source_of_truth: Harvard Health / Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine

transcript_snippet: I just feel healthier when I skip breakfast, honestly, that's just me though, works for me
adjudication_note: Personal preference/anecdote about self, no generalizable checkable claim. Correct behavior is NO extraction.

transcript_snippet: the sun is a star, like literally just a star that happens to be close to us
expected_extraction: The Sun is a star.
adjudication_note: G-type main-sequence star. Baseline sanity-check entry.

transcript_snippet: humans have exactly five senses, five, that's it, sight sound smell taste touch, done
expected_extraction: Humans have exactly five senses.
adjudication_note: Neuroscience recognizes additional senses (balance/vestibular, proprioception, thermoception, etc.); 'exactly five, that's it' is the falsifiable framing.

transcript_snippet: so is coffee, like, actually bad for you or what? I can never keep track of where we landed on coffee
adjudication_note: A question, not an assertion. Correct behavior is NO extraction.

transcript_snippet: Mercury is the closest planet to the sun, um, then Venus, then us
expected_extraction: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
adjudication_note: Standard solar system ordering.

transcript_snippet: water covers like seventy percent of the planet, seventy percent of the surface is ocean basically
expected_extraction: Water covers about 70 percent of the Earth's surface.
adjudication_note: NOAA: about 71% of Earth's surface is water-covered. 'About 70 percent' is accurate.

transcript_snippet: I don't get flu shots because the flu shot literally gives you the flu, that's how they work, they infect you
expected_extraction: The flu shot gives you the flu.
adjudication_note: Injected flu vaccines use inactivated virus or recombinant protein and cannot cause influenza; CDC debunks this explicitly every season.

transcript_snippet: the reason superbugs exist, antibiotic resistance, it's driven by overusing antibiotics, that's the mechanism
expected_extraction: Antibiotic resistance is driven by the overuse of antibiotics.
adjudication_note: CDC and WHO name antibiotic overuse and misuse as the leading driver of resistance.
source_of_truth: CDC Antibiotic Resistance Threats report / WHO

transcript_snippet: humans evolved from chimpanzees, that's evolution, we used to be chimps and then we weren't
expected_extraction: Humans evolved from chimpanzees.
adjudication_note: Humans did not evolve from chimps; both lineages descend from a common ancestor ~6-7 million years ago. Smithsonian debunks this phrasing directly. Misleading defensible; adjudicated False because the stated ancestry relation is contradicted.
source_of_truth: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, Human Origins Program

transcript_snippet: at the top of Everest you're getting like a third of the oxygen you'd get at sea level, a third, that's why they carry tanks
expected_extraction: The summit of Mount Everest has about one-third the oxygen available at sea level.
adjudication_note: Barometric pressure at the summit is roughly a third of sea-level pressure, so available oxygen is about a third. Standard high-altitude physiology figure.
source_of_truth: NIH high-altitude physiology literature / National Geographic

transcript_snippet: if you shave it comes back thicker, everybody knows this, shaving makes the hair grow in thicker and darker
expected_extraction: Shaving makes hair grow back thicker.
adjudication_note: Blunt-cut regrowth feels coarser but shaving does not change hair thickness, color, or growth rate. Debunked in clinical literature since 1928.

transcript_snippet: your heart beats like a hundred thousand times a day, a hundred thousand, just doing its thing
expected_extraction: The human heart beats about 100,000 times a day.
adjudication_note: American Heart Association's standard figure — about 100,000 beats/day at typical resting rates.

transcript_snippet: never eat anything with MSG, MSG is dangerous, it's basically poison for your brain
expected_extraction: MSG in food is dangerous to your health.
adjudication_note: FDA classifies MSG as generally recognized as safe; decades of studies found no consistent harm at food-level doses. The 'Chinese restaurant syndrome' scare is debunked.

transcript_snippet: eat your carrots, carrots give you better eyesight, that's why pilots eat them, improves your vision
expected_extraction: Eating carrots improves your eyesight.
adjudication_note: True element: vitamin A is essential for vision and deficiency harms it. False impression: carrots improve normal sight — a myth amplified by WWII British radar propaganda. Per §4 this is technically-grounded framing creating a wrong impression.
source_of_truth: Harvard Health / Smithsonian Magazine on the WWII carrot myth

transcript_snippet: a glass of red wine a day is actually good for your heart, doctors used to say that all the time, the French thing
expected_extraction: A glass of red wine a day is good for your heart.
adjudication_note: Older observational studies suggested cardiac benefit; newer analyses and WHO's 2023 position hold no level of alcohol is established as safe, and AHA does not recommend drinking for heart health. Genuinely contested and materially incomplete as stated — the §4 NeedsContext case.
source_of_truth: American Heart Association / WHO 2023 statement on alcohol

transcript_snippet: octopuses have three hearts, three actual hearts, and the blood is blue, look it up
expected_extraction: Octopuses have three hearts.
adjudication_note: Two branchial hearts plus one systemic heart. Sounds-fake-but-true entry to balance reflexive debunking.

transcript_snippet: this supplement company did their own internal study and their pill doubles your energy levels, doubles, their research proved it
expected_extraction: A supplement company's internal study proved its pill doubles energy levels.
adjudication_note: An unpublished internal company study is not confirmable or refutable against qualifying sources in real time. Unverifiable is the honest verdict per §3 — not False, since the study's existence and contents can't be checked.

transcript_snippet: wait is it feed a cold starve a fever, or starve a cold feed a fever? I can never remember which way it goes
adjudication_note: A question, not an assertion. Correct behavior is NO extraction.

transcript_snippet: your body is basically water, like sixty percent of you is just water, roughly
expected_extraction: The human body is about 60 percent water.
adjudication_note: USGS and physiology references put adult body water at roughly 55-60% — 'about 60 percent' is the standard figure.
source_of_truth: USGS Water Science School / NIH physiology references
